examples: The internet at our house is really fast.
I buy train tickets on the internet.
인터넷이 안 돼서 일을 못 해요.
The internet is down so I cannot work.
nuance: 인터넷 is the everyday word for the internet as a network, and going online is often said as 인터넷을 하다.
mistakes: Saying 인터넷에 찾아요 instead of 인터넷으로 찾아요 for the means.

nuance: 비밀번호 covers passwords and PIN numbers, and people often shorten it to 비번 in casual speech.
mistakes: Saying 비밀번호가 넣어요 instead of 비밀번호를 넣어요 when you enter it.

examples: 이 앱으로 음식을 시킬 수 있어요.
I can order food with this app.
I want to install a new app.
nuance: 앱 is the short loanword for a mobile application, and the fuller form 어플 is also common.
mistakes: Saying 앱이 열어요 instead of 앱을 열어요 when you open it.

examples: If I watch the screen long my eyes hurt.
nuance: 화면 means the display screen of a phone or monitor, while the physical glass panel itself is 액정.
mistakes: Saying 화면이 봐요 instead of 화면을 봐요 when you look at it.

examples: I charge my phone with the charger.
There is a charger in the bag.
I left the charger at home.
nuance: 충전기 is the device for charging, and the cable part alone is often called the 충전 케이블.
mistakes: Saying 충전기에 충전해요 instead of 충전기로 충전해요 for the tool.

examples: I can use the wifi here.
The wifi is not working so it is frustrating.
nuance: 와이파이 is the everyday loanword for wireless internet, distinct from mobile data which is called 데이터.
mistakes: Saying 와이파이로 연결해요 instead of 와이파이에 연결해요 for connecting.

examples: I can watch videos on my phone.
I watched a fun video today.
nuance: 영상 means a video clip such as one online, while a feature film at the cinema is usually 영화.
mistakes: Saying 영상이 봐요 instead of 영상을 봐요 when you watch it.

examples: I play games on the weekend.
I play games together with a friend.
nuance: 게임 covers video and mobile games, and to play one Koreans say 게임을 하다 rather than a separate verb.
mistakes: Saying 게임을 놀아요 instead of the natural 게임을 해요.

examples: I can do a search on the internet.
I tried searching the restaurant name.
There are too many search results.
nuance: 검색 is the act of searching online, and turning it into a verb gives 검색하다 to look something up.
mistakes: Saying 검색이 해요 instead of 검색을 해요 when you search.

examples: Many notifications come from the morning.
The message notifications do not come.
nuance: 알림 means an app or phone notification, while a formal public announcement is usually called 공지.
mistakes: Saying 알림을 와요 instead of 알림이 와요 when one arrives.

examples: I sent a message to my friend.
nuance: 메시지 covers text and chat messages, and a phone text is also called 문자 in everyday speech.
mistakes: Saying 메시지가 보내요 instead of 메시지를 보내요 when you send it.

examples: I write text with the keyboard.
nuance: 키보드 means a physical or on screen keyboard for typing, while a piano keyboard is also called 건반.
mistakes: Saying 키보드에 써요 instead of 키보드로 써요 for the tool.
